overview: A food chain is one straight-line path of energy flow; a food web is the interconnected network of many overlapping food chains.
genZNote: Food chain: one straight line of who-eats-whom. Food web: the tangled group chat of an entire ecosystem's meals.

aspects.label: Structure
aspects.valueA: A single, linear sequence of organisms, each eating the one before it.
aspects.valueB: A complex, interconnected network of multiple overlapping food chains.

aspects.label: Realism / Complexity
aspects.valueA: A simplified representation, rarely reflecting real ecosystem complexity.
aspects.valueB: A more realistic model, since most organisms eat and are eaten by more than one species.

aspects.label: Ecosystem Stability
aspects.valueA: Disruption of one link can severely affect the whole chain.
aspects.valueB: Generally more resilient — alternative paths can compensate if one link is disrupted.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A food web's greater stability compared to a single food chain is a common conceptual exam point about ecosystem resilience.
overlay.memoryTrick: Chain = one line. Web = many chains tangled together.
overlay.commonMisconception: A food chain isn't 'wrong' or obsolete — it's simply a simplified teaching tool; real ecosystems always function as food webs.
